title: Before You Launch: Is Your Capital Campaign Goal Achievable?
description: A campaign goal needs support from donors, leadership and the organization behind it. Anthony Alonso will walk through the questions a feasibility study should answer before your board commits to a public goal. Learn how donor assessment, confidential interviews and a clear case for support inform the decision to launch, adjust or prepare further.
learning_objectives: Identify the donor, leadership and organizational evidence needed to test a campaign goal.
Explain how confidential interviews and donor assessment inform campaign readiness.
Use feasibility findings to recommend a launch, revised scope or readiness plan.

title: Your Best Legacy Prospects May Already Be Giving You $25
description: Longtime donors can be easy to overlook when gift size drives every prospect list. Jeff Grandy will explain how giving history and loyalty help identify people worth engaging in a legacy conversation. Explore a practical path from donor-file segmentation through personal outreach, qualification and staff follow-up, with clear distinctions between interest, a documented intention and a realized gift.
learning_objectives: Identify loyalty signals that can guide legacy prospect selection.
Outline a respectful qualification conversation and a staff follow-up process.
Distinguish legacy interest, confirmed intentions and realized gifts in program reporting.

title: Too Valuable for a Form Letter, Too Many for Your Major Gift Team
description: Many donors need more personal attention than a broad appeal can provide, while your major gift team has limited capacity. Gwen Paxon will show how a managed mid-level program can give these donors consistent outreach and a clear relationship owner. Explore segmentation, conversation planning and handoffs that help staff focus their time and keep donor follow-up moving.
learning_objectives: Define a mid-level segment using giving history, engagement and staff coverage.
Outline an outreach cadence with assigned relationship ownership.
Set criteria for major gift handoffs and measures of donor engagement.

title: Understanding Latino Philanthropy: Build Trust and Engage More Donors
description: Strong donor relationships begin with listening. Anthony Alonso will explore how family, community, giving motivations and individual language preferences can inform engagement with Latino donors. Learn how to ask better questions and adapt annual fund and mid-level outreach without treating a diverse community as a single donor profile.
learning_objectives: Recognize the limits of assumptions about Latino donors and giving preferences.
Develop questions that surface individual motivations, language preferences and community connections.
Adapt annual fund and mid-level outreach using what donors share.

title: The Feasibility Study Is Finished. How Do You Run the Campaign?
description: A completed study provides direction. Running the campaign requires a working plan, clear responsibilities and steady follow-through. Jeff Grandy will walk through the transition from feasibility findings to campaign implementation, including leadership recruitment, donor strategy, volunteer preparation and progress reviews. Consider where outside campaign counsel can support staff and volunteers while the client leads donor solicitation.
learning_objectives: Translate feasibility findings into campaign priorities, milestones and assignments.
Define staff, volunteer and counsel responsibilities for cultivation and solicitation.
Structure pipeline reviews and leadership follow-up to keep the campaign moving.

title: Latino Philanthropy Across Generations: Building Major and Legacy Gifts
description: Major and legacy gift conversations develop around the people, priorities and impact a donor values. Anthony Alonso will explore approaches to engaging Latino donors and families across generations, with attention to individual preferences and family participation by invitation. Learn how to connect donor interests with cultivation, gift-planning referrals and consistent follow-up. This session can be attended on its own or alongside the April program.
learning_objectives: Use open-ended questions to understand donor interests and desired family involvement.
Plan cultivation steps that reflect each donor's preferences and long-term interests.
Identify when to offer a major gift conversation or a referral to qualified gift-planning advisers.

title: Beyond a Wealth Score: Find the Prospects Who Fit Your Mission
description: A wealth estimate leaves important questions unanswered about a donor's interest in your mission and the next appropriate conversation. Jeff Grandy will show how giving history, affinity, capacity and connections can inform a prioritized research roster. Explore what belongs in an actionable prospect profile, how to validate findings and how research supports relationship managers.
learning_objectives: Combine capacity, affinity, giving history and connections to prioritize prospects.
Identify source-verification and donor-privacy checks for prospect profiles.
Translate research findings into a practical next step for a relationship manager.

title: Legacy Giving Takes More Than a Brochure and a Will Tool
description: A legacy tool or brochure can generate interest, but someone still needs to listen, answer questions and follow up. Gwen Paxon will examine the relationship work that supports a legacy giving program, including qualification calls, referrals, intention documentation and stewardship. Explore how Legacy Call can complement your existing marketing and gift-planning resources.
learning_objectives: Map the follow-up steps between an initial inquiry and a documented intention.
Assign responsibilities for outreach, adviser referrals and donor stewardship.
Choose measures that track conversations and intentions without treating them as realized revenue.

title: Your Capital Campaign Has Stalled. What Will Get It Moving?
description: When a campaign slows, the next step is a clear diagnosis of what is holding it back. Anthony Alonso will examine the case for support, leadership participation, prospect pipeline and follow-through. Learn how to structure a campaign review, set near-term priorities and determine where hands-on counsel can help staff and volunteers rebuild momentum.
learning_objectives: Assess potential barriers in the case, leadership, pipeline and campaign execution.
Prioritize corrective actions using available donor and campaign evidence.
Define a recovery plan with owners, milestones and regular progress reviews.

title: Is Your Annual Fund Leaving Donors and Revenue Behind?
description: Calling can give donors an opportunity to respond, reconnect and share what matters to them. Jeff Grandy will explain how Annual Fund Connect fits alongside mail, email and other donor communications. Learn how to choose renewal and reactivation segments, coordinate messaging, capture useful feedback and evaluate results across channels.
learning_objectives: Select renewal, reactivation and engagement segments for a calling program.
Coordinate calls with mail, email and donor follow-up responsibilities.
Define cross-channel measures for gifts, donor response and relationship outcomes.

title: AI for Smarter Prospect Research and Stronger Donor Follow-Up
description: Fundraising teams can use AI to organize public-source research, prepare staff-reviewed outreach and keep track of next actions. Anthony Alonso will examine practical applications alongside the checks they require. Learn how to verify sources, protect donor information and keep relationship decisions with people. Examples will focus on research and capacity-building workflows rather than promises of automated fundraising results.
learning_objectives: Identify research and follow-up tasks suited to staff-supervised AI support.
Apply source-verification and donor-data safeguards before using AI output.
Design a human review step and a simple evaluation process for an AI-assisted workflow.

title: Close the Gap: A Calling Strategy for Your Campaign’s Final Phase
description: The public phase of a campaign needs a coordinated plan for the donors who have yet to participate. Jeff Grandy will explore how segmented calling, clear messages and timely follow-up can support campaign wrap-up. Learn how to connect broad-based outreach with the campaign's remaining priorities while protecting ongoing major gift conversations.
learning_objectives: Identify donor segments and messages appropriate for campaign wrap-up calling.
Coordinate calling activity with staff, volunteers and active major gift relationships.
Define follow-up assignments and measures for participation and campaign progress.
